newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN BASE METALS STEADY, INDUSTRIAL DEMAND SLOW.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN BASE METALS STEADY, INDUSTRIAL DEMAND SLOW.

text.p: Base metals' prices held steady in a narrow band on the local market, dealer said.

Industrial demand remained sluggish but limited supplies and reports of firm trend in the world market kept offerings at a low ebb. Copper was quiet at 13,200 rupees per quintal, as was zinc at 8,400 rupees and lead at 4,200 rupees per quintal.
"Inflow of imported metals is low and looking at the uptrend in the world market, local prices may move up on fresh buying," said Sharad Parikh, president of Bombay Metal Exchange.
Amid nominal trading, aluminium was indicated at 7,800 rupees per quintal, tin at 29,200 rupees and nickel at 34,100 rupees, all unchanged.
